audit.whatIsWrong: Sap Magic is never mentioned in either layer, and the entry's central instruction is to poke him from maximum Tongue Lash range.
audit.why: Riot's text: "Maokai's basic attack also heals him and deals additional damage on a moderate cooldown. Each time Maokai casts a spell or is struck by an enemy's spell, this cooldown is reduced." Every Tongue Lash that lands accelerates his healing passive. The entry's whole plan — sit at 900 and chip — actively funds the thing that beats it. This is the highest-value fact in the matchup and it is absent. _missing-interactions.json also flags needs-antiheal here, and the content layer never mentions Grievous Wounds at all.
audit.corrected: Being struck by a spell shortens Sap Magic's cooldown. Free poke is not free against Maokai — prefer autos for stacks, and treat Grievous Wounds as the item that actually breaks the stalemate.

audit.whatIsWrong: Twisted Advance is described as an escape in wants.you[2] and wants.foe[2] ("root-escape the moment you commit your combo", "so he has no root to escape the swallow"), while `late` says he "has no dash or escape". The entry contradicts itself and both readings are wrong.
audit.why: Riot's text: "Maokai contorts into a mass of moving roots, becoming untargetable and dashing to the target. Upon arrival, he roots the target." It is a targeted dash toward an enemy — it can only ever close distance, never break away. The real interaction is the untargetable window: Devour is point-and-click, so casting it as he starts Twisted Advance throws the ultimate away. _missing-interactions.json flags exactly this (untargetable-dodges-burst) and neither layer mentions it.
audit.corrected: Twisted Advance dashes toward you and he is untargetable for the flight. It is an engage, not an escape. Do not spend Devour on the cast — wait until he arrives.

audit.whatIsWrong: Sapling Toss's range is never given, and the entry repeatedly advises playing at maximum Tongue Lash range as if that is outside his reach.
audit.why: Sapling Toss is 1100 range against Tongue Lash's 900. He out-ranges your only poke tool by 200 units on an 18s cooldown, and the kit notes saplings are "More effective in brush". So the "fish stacks at max Q range" plan puts you inside his zoning tool while staying outside your own commit range.
audit.corrected: Sapling Toss reaches 1100 to your 900 — max Tongue Lash range is inside his zoning, not outside it.
sources: champ-data/_kits/maokai.json — Sapling Toss range 1100; champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json — Tongue Lash range 900

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry says "respect the cooldown" and "play around his W cooldown" repeatedly without ever giving a number, in either layer.
audit.why: Twisted Advance is 14/13/12/11/10s, Bramble Smash 7/6.5/6/5.5/5s, Sapling Toss 18/17/16/15/14s, Nature's Grasp 130/110/90s. "Respect the cooldown" is not actionable; "fourteen seconds at rank one" is. The whole matchup is a stalemate broken by who commits into whose spent window.
audit.corrected: Twisted Advance 14s at rank 1 down to 10s. Bramble Smash 7s. Sapling Toss 18s. Nature's Grasp 130s at rank 1.

audit.whatIsWrong: content `mid` and whys[4] use "Abyssal Voyage" as the level-6 plan.
audit.why: Tahm Kench has no Abyssal Voyage — W is Abyssal Dive, R is Devour. whys[4] makes it the entire reason to roam at 6, which leaves the stage unexplained once the ability is removed.
audit.corrected: Level 6 is about Nature's Grasp on 130s and Devour arriving, not a global relocate.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json — W Abyssal Dive, R Devour

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2], spikes[3], whys[6] and full tradeGood/dosFull all describe a "3-stack stun into Devour" sequence.
audit.why: Tongue Lash at three stacks stuns and consumes the stacks; Devour needs three stacks to fire. The two compete for the same resource. Against an immobile tank whose only mobility dashes toward you, Devour is the correct spend every time.
audit.corrected: Three stacks buys the stun or the swallow, not both. Take Devour.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json — An Acquired Taste, Tongue Lash

audit.whatIsWrong: content `early` states flatly that "Maokai at level 1 cannot root you — his W is level 2".
audit.why: Nothing prevents a Maokai from ranking Twisted Advance at level 1; it is a convention, not a rule. Stating it as a fact invites a player to walk into a level-1 root they were told was impossible. I softened rather than reversed it, since typical skill order is not in the kit file and I did not verify it.
audit.corrected: Phrase it as a tendency: he almost never takes Twisted Advance at 1.
sources: champ-data/_kits/maokai.json — no rank restriction on Twisted Advance

edits.before: Maokai at level 1 cannot root you — his W is level 2 — so use that window aggressively: land Tongue Lash to slow him whenever he steps up to plant a sapling, and let Thick Skin passively convert whatever poke he does get through. You are not trying to kill him, just establish that he cannot freely farm from brush. The moment he hits level 2 his W root dash changes the equation entirely: if you are in melee range when it lands he locks you in place for a full sapling burst, so respect the cooldown and keep your stacks on him from Q range rather than trading autos.
edits.after: Maokai almost never takes Twisted Advance at 1, so use that window: land Tongue Lash to slow him whenever he steps up to plant a sapling, and let Thick Skin convert whatever poke he gets through. Know what your poke costs, though — Sap Magic's cooldown falls every time he casts a spell and every time an enemy spell strikes him, so your own Q is part-funding his heals. Once Twisted Advance is ranked it dashes at you and he is untargetable for the flight, which means the cast is the tell and the landing is the punish window, not the other way round.

edits.before: Levels 4 through 6 are the flattest part of this matchup — both of you are unkillable but neither of you is threatening. Maokai can wall you off with sapling placement in brushes and you cannot reliably reach him without burning Flash into his W root. Fish for An Acquired Taste stacks at maximum Tongue Lash range and play around his W cooldown: the instant it is down, step forward aggressively to bait the engagement or commit your Q-stun into Devour before it resets. At level 6 your Abyssal Voyage gives you global threat he cannot match, but his Nature's Grasp ultimate provides its own engage tool in teamfights — call your jungler or roam rather than trying to force a solo kill.
edits.after: Levels 4 through 6 are the flattest part of this matchup — both of you are unkillable but neither of you is threatening. Sapling Toss reaches 1100 against your 900, so he zones you from outside your only poke tool and the brush makes it worse. Play around Twisted Advance, which is 14s at rank 1 and 10s at rank 5: the instant it is spent, step up and commit your three stacks to Devour — never to the Tongue Lash stun, which consumes exactly the same three. At level 6 Nature's Grasp is 130s and hands him a teamfight engage you cannot match at range, so call your jungler or take the wave rather than forcing a solo kill.

edits.before: At 2-plus items the matchup swings your way because Maokai's immobility becomes a liability rather than a neutral. A fully stacked 3-stack stun into Devour removes him from a teamfight entirely and he has no dash or escape to prevent it — he either commits his W root before you stack him, which burns his only engage, or he stands in place and gets swallowed. Thick Skin grey-health at this stage absorbs his sapling chip almost entirely, so he cannot whittle you down before you reach him. Play the frontline and peel your carries; his value is in landing his own engage before you land yours.
edits.after: At 2-plus items the matchup swings your way because Twisted Advance only ever dashes toward a target — it is an engage, not an escape, so he cannot use it to break away once you hold three stacks. Devour removes him from a teamfight entirely, and the Q stun would spend those same three stacks, so hold them. Grievous Wounds matters more here than another tank stat: Sap Magic heals off his attacks and speeds up every time a spell touches him. Play the frontline and peel your carries; his value is landing his engage before you land yours.

edits.after: Tongue Lash slows him off sapling-planting, but every spell that strikes Maokai shortens Sap Magic — free poke is not actually free here.

notes: Two facts carry this matchup and neither was anywhere in the entry. First, Sap Magic's cooldown is reduced every time an enemy spell strikes Maokai — so the entry's core instruction (poke from max Tongue Lash range) is directly feeding his sustain. Second, Twisted Advance is a targeted dash toward you with an untargetable flight, which makes it an engage rather than the escape the entry twice calls it, and makes it a Devour-eater if you cast on the animation. The full layer already prescribes anti-heal in breakdown.late; the content layer never mentions it, which is why I moved Grievous Wounds into spikes[2] and `late`. No chart edits needed here — 51.59% against a 2/2/3 split is one of the few internally consistent charts in this slice.
